title: A Treasure Map Points to Missing Fossils
summary:
Fossils show us life from millions of years ago. But turning into a fossil is very rare, so only a tiny number of creatures have been saved. Scientists can only find one where the rock is open to view.

That leaves big gaps in what we know about life long ago. Some times and places have given us lots of fossils, others almost none. Digging takes time and money, so knowing where to look helps.

Two scientists have made a tool to help. Thomas A. Neubauer and Mathias Harzhauser studied shallow-sea fossils from the past 540 million years, and mapped where fossil clues are missing.

They used the Paleobiology Database, a huge free list of fossil finds. They also looked at rocks that could hold more fossils.

The results were a surprise. The oldest times have already been studied a lot, and the best chances for new finds are in more recent times: the Cenozoic Era, which began 66 million years ago.

Scientists marked spots where unknown fossils are most likely. Their map helps fossil hunters plan better digs.
why_it_matters: Fossils are like a time machine that shows you what animals looked like millions of years before you were born, and new finds could add missing pages to that story.
